JUDGMENT
The charge sheet is submitted by the PI of CCB police against the accused persons for the offences punishable under section 420 of IPC & Sec.192(A), (5), 192(B) of Karnataka Land Revenue Act 1984.

2. The prosecution case in brief is as under :
That the accused no.2 with an intention to illegally earn money, started M/s.Graniti Properties Pvt., Ltd., at No.3, 3rd cross, 10th A Main, 2nd stage, Indiranagar and purchased agricultural land in Sy.No.183, 184, 185 from CW 2 to 7 and executed GPA/Agreement with them.
Further, the accused no.2 collected money from customers by saying that he will form sites in the said agricultural land in the name of European Township.

Further, the accused no.2 entered into Memorandum of Understanding with CW 9-Managing Director of Orange Properties with regard to marketing of said sites by announcing the free offer of a Maruthi 800 car to the customers who will purchase 30x40 site and free offer of a Maruthi swift car to the customers who will purchase 60 x 40 sites and etc.,

In this regard, the accused persons collected Rs.5,32,000/- from CW 1 and entered into sale agreement with regard to sites No.316 & 317 situated at Erandahalli, Hoskote taluk, thereafter neither allotted site nor returned the money paid by the CW 1, thereby cheated the CW 1.

Thus, the accused persons used the agricultural land to non-agricultural purposes,
without any Order for any Land Transformation.

Thereby the accused persons have committed the offences punishable under section 420 of IPC & Sec.192(A), (5),
192(B) of Karnataka Land Revenue Act 1984.
3. The complainant has given complaint to the Ashoknagar police station and accordingly the police have registered the case in crime No.381/2009.
The concerned police after completing the investigation have filed charge sheet against the accused.
4. On the receipt of charge sheet the cognizance was taken.
The prosecution papers are given to the accused no.2.
The charge was framed and read over to the accused.
The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried, accordingly the plea of the accused no.2 was recorded.

5. The prosecution in support of their case have got examined 6 witnesses as PW 1 to 6 and got marked 5 document at Ex.P.1 to 5.
6.
The statement of accused no.2 U/s 313 of Cr.P.C is recorded.
The accused denied the incriminating evidence and has not chosen to adduce defence evidence on his behalf.

The points that arise for consideration is as under :
1.

Whether prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that the accused no.2 with an intention to illegally earn money, started M/s.Graniti Properties Pvt., Ltd., at No.3, 3rd cross, 10th A Main, 2nd stage, Indiranagar and purchased agricultural to 7 and executed GPA/Agreement with them.
Further, the accused no.2 collected money from customers by saying that he will form sites in the said land in the name of European Township.

Further, the accused no.2 entered into Memorandum of Understanding with CW 9-MD of Orange Properties with regard to marketing of said sites by announcing the free offer of a Maruthi 800 car to the customers who will purchase 30x40 site and free offer of a Maruthi swift car to the customers who will purchase 60 x 40 sites and etc.,

In this regard, the accused persons collected Rs.5,32,000/-
from CW1 and entered into sale agreement situated at Erandahalli, Hoskote taluk, thereafter without allotting the site and without returning the money paid by him, cheated the CW 1.
Thus, the accused persons used the agricultural land to non agricultural purposes, without any Order for any Land Transformation.
Thus the accused has committed the offences punishable under section 420 of IPC & Sec.192(A), (5), 192(B) of Karnataka Land Revenue Act 1984 and within my cognizance ?
2. What order ?

sentences.text: 11. In order to prove the allegations made against the accused, prosecution has got examined the complainant/victim - Roopali Singhal as Pw.2 and got marked the complaint at Ex.P.4.

She has deposed that during 2007, on going through the advertisement, on 29/6/08 she has invested Rs.5,32,000/- through cheques towards purchase of 2 sites to the accused company and received receipts for the same.
But thereafter, as the accused failed to get the approvals, she sought to cancel her bookings and return money.
Thereafter, the accused persons neither returned her money nor allotted any sites to her, hence, she lodged the complaint as per Ex.P.4.

But during the course of cross examination by the learned counsel for accused, the PW 2 has deposed as hereunder :
" I have not seen the accused at the time of transaction."

12. Further, in order to prove the allegations made against the accused, prosecution has got examined the victim Nanjappa-CW 2 as PW 3, he has deposed that the accused persons purchased the agricultural land in Sy.No.67 from him and they entered into an agreement in that regard and accused persons paid Rs.5 lakhs cash to him and also issued cheque for Rs.5 lakhs, when he presented the said cheque for encashment, it was bounced.
He further deposed that thereafter the CCB police have enquired him and recorded his statement.

But during the course of cross examination by the learned counsel for accused, the PW 3 has deposed as hereunder :
"

The PW 3 being the victim has given clear goby to his chief examination by saying that he could not identify the accused no.2.
This evidence of PW 3 is not helpful to the prosecution to prove the guilt against the accused.
13. The prosecution has further got examined CW 4- Mohan as PW 1, who has deposed about entering into agreement with accused persons with regard to property in Sy.No.39/4 of Heerandahalli village.

Further, the CW12-Gajendra is examined as PW4, he has deposed about CW 13 entrusting the job of land procurement at Heerandahalli to accused no.2 and accused no.2 without the knowledge of CW 13, purchased some sites to his personal gain.
The cross examination of PW 1 & 4 was deferred.
Thereafter they did not tender themselves for cross-examination.

14. Further, the prosecution got examined CW3- Kumaraswamy as PW 5, he has deposed about entering into an agreement with accused persons with regard to site in Sy.No.184 of Heerandahalli and about giving statement before CCB police.

sentences.text: The PW 5 being the victim has given clear goby to his chief examination by saying that he could not identify the accused no.2.
This evidence of PW 5 creates doubt in the mind of this court and it is not helpful to the prosecution to prove the guilt against the accused.
15. PW 6, who is the police official witness has supported the case of the prosecution.

Though the PW 1 & 4 have supported the case of the prosecution in their chief examination, it is significant to note here that they have not tendered themselves for cross examination inspite of issuance of number of summons, NBW and proclamation, therefore, on 02/09/2024 this court dropped them.
The main material witnesses ie., PW 3 & 5 turned hostile to the case of the prosecution and have not identified the accused.
Nothing is uttered by the PW 3 & 5 in order to support the prosecution case.

16. In the present case on hand the important material witnesses/victims themselves have turned hostile and have not supported the case of prosecution and accordingly prosecution has utterly failed to prove the case beyond all reasonable doubt.
The evidence of other witnesses will not help the prosecution to prove the guilt against the accused.
Hence, it cannot be held that the accused no.2 has committed the offences punishable under section 420 of IPC & Sec.192(A), (5), 192(B) of Karnataka Land Revenue Act 1984.
Accordingly I answered this point in the Negative.

17. Point No.2 :- In view the findings given in point No.1, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER Acting under section 248(1) of Cr.P.C accused no.2 is hereby Acquitted for the offences punishable under section 420 of IPC & Sec.192(A), (5), 192(B) of Karnataka Land Revenue Act 1984.
The bail bond and surety bond of accused no.2 stands canceled after appeal period is over.
